name: Design cement slurries and run lab tests
summary: Each casing string needs a cement slurry that stays pumpable long enough to be placed at the well's temperature and pressure, then sets hard enough to seal the well and meet the AER's strength rule. A technical sales engineer takes the producer's request, a cement engineer works out temperatures, cement tops and volumes and models placement, and laboratory technologists mix the proposed blend with the rig's water and test thickening time, fluid loss, free water, rheology and compressive strength before a lab supervisor signs the report and the engineer issues the cement program. The work is rushed because rigs give one to three days' notice, well data such as the caliper log arrive late, tests run overnight on a limited number of consistometers, and about one design in five needs its retarder adjusted and the test rerun.

baseline.org_archetype: A Canadian pressure pumping company running about 16 cementing units from Alberta and northeast BC district bases with bulk blending plants, plus a Calgary cement and fluids laboratory and engineering office.
baseline.notes: Common practice of large WCSB cementing service lines in 2019-2022: dispatch board and phone, ERP inventory, tablet field tickets, lab database and spreadsheets, cement placement software; no automated blending recipe download or live job data streaming to the office as standard.

unit_of_work: one cement design (one casing string for one well or a repeat design for a pad)
trigger: A producer or the district sends a job request with well data for an upcoming intermediate, production or liner cement job, or a surface job in a new area.
end_state: A lab-approved cement program and slurry design issued to the field and bulk plant and the lab report sent to the producer; or the design shelved because the job was cancelled or lost.

volume.seasonality: Follows the rig count: heaviest from December to March, lightest during spring break-up.

evidence.note: Kept the organisation file's 250 designs a month against about 400 jobs: surface jobs in known areas and repeat wells on a pad reuse an existing design; cementing activity tracks the rig count (src3).
Request intake and sending programs to the producer, about 30 minutes a design; estimate.
About 3.5 engineering hours a design over 250 designs (about 6.7 FTE); these are the cement engineers among the organisation file's 16 completions design engineers; estimate.
About 5 hands-on hours a design including retests (about 9.6 FTE at 130 productive hours); the lab runs extended hours; estimate.
Review and sign-off of every lab report, about 20 minutes each plus queries; estimate.

systems.name: Email, Microsoft Teams and mobile phones
Fracture and cement placement modelling software
Laboratory test records (lab database and spreadsheets)

resources.name: Ultrasonic cement analyser and curing chambers for strength tests

steps.name: Receive and log the job request
steps.description: The technical sales engineer receives the request by email or phone from the producer's drilling engineer or the district, enters the well, casing string, expected job date and rig in the design tracker, and forwards it to the cement engineer for the area.

error.defect_description: Job date or casing string recorded wrongly

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB cementing and oilfield laboratory practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Check well data are complete
steps.description: The cement engineer checks the request for depths, hole and casing sizes, bottom-hole temperature, mud type and weight, required cement top, water source and any lost-circulation history, and lists what is missing.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB cementing and oilfield laboratory practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Request missing well data
steps.description: The engineer emails or phones the producer's drilling engineer for the missing items, most often the bottom-hole temperature, the expected caliper or the water source.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB cementing and oilfield laboratory practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Wait for producer data
steps.description: The producer gathers the data from its drilling team or the rig and sends them back; the caliper log only exists once the hole is logged, often a day before the job.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB cementing and oilfield laboratory practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Look up proven designs for the area
steps.description: The engineer searches the lab database and past programs for slurries already tested at similar depth and temperature for the same producer and formation, and decides whether one can be reused with only a field blend check.

error.defect_description: Design reused at a temperature outside its tested range

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB cementing and oilfield laboratory practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Calculate temperatures, cement tops and volumes
steps.description: The engineer works out circulating and static temperatures, takes the required cement top from the AER township figure or the licence, calculates slurry volumes from hole size with the required excess, and sets the strength target at the uppermost hydrocarbon zone.

error.defect_description: Temperature or cement top error carried into the test schedule

control.basis: AER Directive 009 items 9-12 and 24: required cement top, caliper volume plus at least 20% excess, 3,500 kPa in 48 hours at the uppermost hydrocarbon zone temperature (4.4 C surface, 2.7 C/100 m when unknown)

evidence.note: Directive 009 requirements on cement tops, volumes and strength (src1); times are estimates.

steps.name: Model slurry placement
steps.description: The engineer runs the placement simulator with the proposed spacer, lead and tail slurries and pump rates to check equivalent circulating density against fracture pressure, mud removal and the job time the slurry must cover.

error.defect_description: Job time underestimated, so the thickening time target is too short

evidence.note: Engineers use simulation software for slurry placement and temperature (src2); times are estimates.

steps.name: Write the lab test request
steps.description: The engineer enters the recipe, test temperature and pressure schedule, thickening time window, fluid loss and strength targets in the lab database, and says whether a water sample from the rig is needed.

error.defect_description: Test schedule keyed for the wrong depth

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB cementing and oilfield laboratory practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Wait for rig water sample
steps.description: The rig or a district truck sends a jug of the mix water to the lab by courier or hot-shot; samples from remote leases can take a day or more to arrive.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB cementing and oilfield laboratory practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Log samples and prepare materials
steps.description: A laboratory technologist logs the request and samples, draws cement of the right class and lot and the additives from lab stock, weighs them for the test batch and analyses the water if it is new.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB cementing and oilfield laboratory practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Run thickening time test
steps.description: The technologist mixes the slurry in the lab blender, loads it in the high-pressure consistometer, runs the temperature and pressure schedule and watches until the slurry reaches the end point, usually 70 Bearden units.

error.defect_description: Wrong schedule loaded on the consistometer

evidence.note: Thickening time test method and end point (src5); queue for consistometers and times are estimates.

steps.name: Test fluid loss, free water and rheology
steps.description: While the consistometer runs, the technologist conditions further batches and runs the fluid loss test for 30 minutes, sets up the two-hour free water test in a cylinder and reads rheology on the viscometer.
outputs: fluid loss, free water and rheology results

evidence.note: Test durations from the cement testing guide (src5).

steps.name: Compare results with design targets
steps.description: The technologist compares thickening time with the job time plus safety margin and checks fluid loss, free water and rheology against the targets; if thickening time is off, they adjust retarder or accelerator and rerun.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB cementing and oilfield laboratory practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Set up compressive strength test
steps.description: The technologist pours cubes for a crush test or loads the ultrasonic cement analyser at the strength-test temperature; when a tested system already covers the condition or the rig is calling, strength results from the library are used.

evidence.note: Crush tests after 8, 16 or 24 hours and UCA runs of about 24 hours (src5); split is an estimate.

steps.name: Read strength results
steps.description: After the cure the technologist reads the strength curve or crushes the cubes and checks the slurry reaches the 3,500 kPa requirement within 48 hours at the zone temperature and the producer's own wait-on-cement target.

control.basis: AER Directive 009 item 11: at least 3,500 kPa after 48 hours at the temperature of the uppermost hydrocarbon-bearing zone when fillers are used

evidence.note: Strength requirement (src1) and test durations (src5); failure share is an estimate.

steps.name: Enter results and draft the lab report
steps.description: The technologist enters all results in the lab database, attaches the consistometer chart and strength curve, and generates the lab report with the final recipe and test conditions.

error.defect_description: Result transcribed wrongly from the instrument printout

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB cementing and oilfield laboratory practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Review and sign the lab report
steps.description: The lab supervisor checks the test schedule matches the well, the charts support the reported values and the recipe matches what was tested, then signs the report or sends it back for a retest.

control.basis: Company laboratory quality procedure: second-person review and sign-off of every cement lab report

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB cementing and oilfield laboratory practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Write the cement program
steps.description: The engineer writes the cement program: pump schedule, spacer and slurry volumes and densities, displacement, expected pressures, cement tops and the blend sheet for the bulk plant, using the signed lab results.

error.defect_description: Blend sheet additive percentages differ from the tested recipe

evidence.note: Engineers prepare cement programs covering coverage, bonding and strength (src2); times are estimates.

steps.name: Send program and lab report to the producer
steps.description: The technical sales engineer emails the program, lab report and price estimate to the producer's drilling engineer and follows up by phone when the job is close.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB cementing and oilfield laboratory practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Producer reviews the program
steps.description: The producer's drilling engineer reviews volumes, cement tops and slurry choice against its own well plan and approves, asks for changes, or cancels when the well is deferred or awarded elsewhere.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB cementing and oilfield laboratory practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Adapt a proven program
steps.description: For a reusable design the engineer copies the earlier program, updates depths, volumes, temperatures and cement tops for this well, and checks the tested thickening time still covers the job time.

error.defect_description: Old volumes or depths left in the copied program

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB cementing and oilfield laboratory practice in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Issue the program to the field
steps.description: The engineer issues the approved program to the district cementing supervisor and dispatch and the slurry design and blend sheet to the bulk plant, and files them with the lab report.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB cementing and oilfield laboratory practice in 2019-2022.

exceptions.name: Well data missing
exceptions.description: Temperature, caliper or water source missing and requested from the producer.

exceptions.name: Proven design reused
exceptions.description: A design already tested for the area is adapted without new pilot tests; the field blend check in the bulk plant process still applies.

exceptions.name: Thickening time off target
exceptions.description: Retarder or accelerator adjusted and the thickening time test rerun, often overnight.

exceptions.name: Strength too low
exceptions.description: The slurry misses the strength requirement and is redesigned.

exceptions.name: Producer changes
exceptions.description: The producer asks for different volumes, cement tops or slurry and the program is rewritten.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from job request to program issued
benchmarks.population: WCSB intermediate and production cement designs, 2019-2022

evidence.note: Estimate: rigs give one to three days' notice, a thickening time test takes most of a shift and strength tests about 24 hours (src5 gives test durations); long tails come from water samples in transit and retests.

benchmarks.unit: hours of consistometer time per test

evidence.note: Test method from src5; duration is an estimate from typical job times of 3 to 6 hours plus heat-up.

benchmarks.unit: kPa after 48 hours at uppermost hydrocarbon zone temperature
benchmarks.population: Alberta production and intermediate casing slurries with fillers

evidence.note: Directive 009 item 11 (src1).

pain_points.description: Short notice from rigs pushes tests into overnight runs and leaves little time for a retest when thickening time misses.

evidence.note: Typical WCSB practice; the organisation file describes the same pressure.

pain_points.description: Lab-mixed slurries behave differently from field-mixed slurries, so pilot results do not always predict the job.

evidence.note: Field mixing shear differs from lab blenders and changes free water and other properties (src4).

pain_points.description: Well data and rig water samples arrive late, delaying the start of testing.

evidence.note: Caliper logs only exist once the hole is logged; estimate.

pain_points.description: Recipes are typed into the lab database, the program and the blend sheet separately.

evidence.note: Typical period practice without integrated recipe management.

sources.title: Directive 009: Casing Cementing Minimum Requirements (edition of May 14, 2025)
sources.supports: Licensee is responsible for satisfactory cementing. Surface casing cemented full length; if returns are not obtained or the annular level drops, the cement top must be determined and the AER contacted about remedial action (items 4-5). Surface casing centralized top, bottom and every 50 m (item 7). Production and intermediate cement volume from caliper log plus at least 20% excess (item 10). Fillers allowed only if compressive strength is at least 3,500 kPa after 48 hours at the temperature of the uppermost hydrocarbon zone, using 4.4 C surface and 2.7 C/100 m where unknown (items 11-12). Flow returns visually monitored during cementing; cement-top log and remedial program to the AER within 60 days of rig release when returns are missing (item 15). Full details recorded on tour reports or a casing cement report (item 16). Required cement tops by township from figure 1 (items 9, 24). The 2025 edition only adds brine-hosted minerals to the 2022 edition; the same requirements applied in 2019-2022.

sources.title: Cementing
sources.supports: Cement programs prepared by engineers using simulation software for slurry placement, sheath integrity, wellbore properties and temperature; pre-flushes and spacers; surface, intermediate, production, liner, horizontal, plug, remedial and squeeze cementing; lost-circulation blends for the WCSB; R&D facilities and operational support laboratories with lab technicians.

sources.title: Management's Discussion and Analysis for the year ended December 31, 2022
sources.supports: Cementing activity tracks the WCSB rig count (201 rigs in Q4 2022, 176 in Q4 2021); 17 cementing units operated in Q4 2022; annual average of 16 cementing units in the field in 2021 and 2022; cementing about 16-19% of revenue; 1,335,000 tonnes of proppant pumped in 2022 and 1,364,000 in 2021; oilfield cement and proppant sourced from suppliers in Canada and the United States.

sources.title: Shear rate has greater influence on cement slurry properties than total mixing energy
sources.publisher: Oil & Gas Journal (Paul Padgett, Halliburton Energy Services)
sources.supports: Bulk-blend samples taken from the conveying line during blending and mixed in the lab with the actual mixing water under the API procedure; field mixing equipment runs at lower shear than lab blenders, so field slurry properties (free water especially) often differ from lab values; thickening time and fluid loss changed only slightly with mixing energy.

sources.title: Oil Well Cement Testing Simple Guide
sources.supports: Thickening time in an HPHT consistometer (70 Bc end point, some operators 50 Bc); crush tests on moulded cubes after 8, 16 or 24 hours; ultrasonic cement analyser runs usually about 24 hours; fluid loss collected for 30 minutes at circulating temperature; free water test stands about two hours; rheology on a Fann viscometer for displacement and ECD modelling.

assumptions: Loaded hourly costs and headcounts are taken from the organisation file (wage x 1.35).
The organisation file has no cement engineer role; the design-engineer role (completions design engineer) is used for the cement engineers who design slurries and write programs, about 7 of the 16.
A quarter of requests come directly from the producer's drilling engineer rather than through dispatch; this producer link is not in the organisation file.

Compressive strength results take about a day; when the rig is ready the program is issued on library strength data and the fresh result follows, so only 45% of designs wait for a fresh strength result.
The field blend confirmation test is counted in the bulk blending and delivery process, not here.
The share of thickening time retests (22%) is an estimate; a figure of about 25% repeat testing appears in industry literature that was not opened, so it is not cited.

The organisation file models the laboratory as three facilities; a single test ties up an instrument, not a lab, so consistometers (count 10) and strength analysers (count 8) are added as resources the organisation file lacks; counts are estimates.
The simulated median is compared with a tier C benchmark only.
